subject: MQM scanning for additional QTL and estimating QTL effects

messages.author: ae4e3267fde51265
messages.subject: MQM scanning for additional QTL and estimating QTL effects
parts:
Dr. Broman, 

I have set up a multiple QTL mapping model, and I am having trouble deciding whether an additional QTL can be added. 

This is what I have: I started with the QTL that had the highest LOD score in the single QTL scan...
> map_atham=sim.geno(map_atham, step=2, n.draws=128, err=0.001)

> qtl=makeqtl(map_atham, chr = c(4), pos = c(81.2))
> qtl
  QTL object containing imputed genotypes, with 128 imputations. 

     name chr    pos n.gen
Q1 4...@81.2   4 81.157     3

> out.fq=fitqtl(map_atham, qtl=qtl, formula=y~Q1)
Warning message:
In fitqtlengine(pheno = pheno, qtl = qtl, covar = covar, formula = formula,  :
  Dropping 38 individuals with missing phenotypes.

> summary(out.fq)

fitqtl summary

Method: multiple imputation 
Model:  normal phenotype
Number of observations : 138 

Full model result
----------------------------------  
Model formula: y ~ Q1 

       df        SS        MS      LOD     %var Pvalue(Chi2)    Pvalue(F)
Model   2  245.6611 122.83054 3.210181 10.15878  0.000616338 0.0007237782
Error 135 2172.5532  16.09299                                            
Total 137 2418.2143 


> out.aq <- addqtl(map_atham, qtl=rqtl, formula=y~Q1)
Warning message:
In addqtl(map_atham, qtl = rqtl, formula = y ~ Q1) :
  Dropping 38 individuals with missing phenotypes.

> max(out.aq, chr = c(2,3,4))
                    chr pos  lod
29.1_CHR_4_20504180   3  81 2.72
> plot(out.aq, chr = c(2,3,4), ylab="LOD score")

When I search for new additional QTLs, I get 29.1_CHR_4_20504 marker that has an LOD score of 2.72, and adding this in the QTL model increases the LOD score of the model. I assumed that I need to compare this to the penalized LOD score, but I could not find this in the book. 

I also had a question about estimating QTL effects. Below is the code I used for estimating the effects, and although I read the section about estimating QTL effects, I'm still having trouble interpreting the results. I would love any guidance/direction on this. Thank you so much! 

> out.fq2<- fitqtl(map_atham, qtl=qtl, formula=y~Q1,dropone=FALSE, get.ests=TRUE)
Warning message:
In fitqtlengine(pheno = pheno, qtl = qtl, covar = covar, formula = formula,  :
  Dropping 38 individuals with missing phenotypes.

> summary(out.fq2)

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] MQM scanning for additional QTL and estimating QTL effects
parts:
I would compare the maximum lod score from addqtl() to the scanone()
permutation results.

The a and d coefficients are the usual "additive" and "dominance"
effects in an intercross. a = half the differences between the phenotype
averages for the two homozygotes, and d = difference between the
phenotype average for the heterozygotes and the average of the two
homozygote averages.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] MQM scanning for additional QTL and estimating QTL effects
parts:
It would be helpful if you provided an example to show exactly what you're looking at, but I take it you're looking at a 4-way cross. We treat that as the parents being AB x CD, so the offspring genotypes are AC, BC, AD, BD. The intercept is then the estimated average phenotype for the AC genotype, and the BC,AD,BD coefficients are for the differences between the average phenotype for these genotypes and the average phenotype for the AC genotype.

karl
